newsitem.title: USA: CME to seek CFTC okay on smaller Eurodlr tick size.
newsitem.headline: CME to seek CFTC okay on smaller Eurodlr tick size.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange said Thursday it will seek approval to halve and, in some cases quarter, the tick size in its interest rate futures.

In floor notice to members, the CME said its board Wednesday decided to seek Commodity Futures Trading Commission approval to halve the minimum price increment in the serial and the first through fourth quarterly expiration months in its Eurodollar futures and futures-options. It wants half-tick trading in all LIBOR and Treasury bill futures and options.
Until recently, all CME interest rate futures were quoted in full basis points, or increments of 0.01 each worth $25.00.
The CME already has tested half-ticks, or 0.005 basis points each worth $12.50, with some expiring Eurodollar futures during their delivery months.

The CME said that, pending further review by its board, it wants to enact 60 days after the first half-ticks take effect a further cut in the minimum price move to quarter-ticks, or 0.0025 basis points worth $6.25 each, in the serial and nearest March quarterly Eurodollar futures and options.
Under the same time frame, CME said it also wants half-tick trading in Eurodollar so-called "red" contract months, or the fifth through eighth quarterly months.

At the same time, CME plans to move to quarter-tick trading in Eurodollar "pack" combinations and adopt quarter-tick trading for LIBOR, Federal funds and Treasury bill futures and options comparable to their Eurodolalr counterparts.

The board also convened a special task force and advisory council on interest rates to report to the board within 90 days on issues such as contract specifications, pit size, pit trading mechanics and costs, hedging alternatives, and technology issues including hand-held devices and electronic order entry, the floor notice stated.

"It has always been central to the character of our institution to be at the forefront of change," said chairman Jack Sandner and president Rick Kilcollin in the notice. "This has been stressed repeatedly over the course of several open meeting with members of the Eurodollar pit community."

In a separate notice, the board approved temporarily delisting December 1997 13-week U.S. Treasury bill futures and options months. It said there currently is no open interest in these contracts and that it intends to relist the 13-week T-bill contract as a cash-settled product beginning with the December 1997 contract month "at a date in the near future."
